origin: 404 is the HTTP status code a web server returns when it can't find a page at the requested address, which is why this screen is commonly called a 404 page.
whenToUse: People arrive at a page whose address changed or that was deleted.
Many people come from outside links or old bookmarks.
There's a way to find it again within the site.
whenNotToUse: The page can't be viewed for lack of permission (use permission denied).
The service is under maintenance (use a maintenance page).
You know the new address (redirect straight to it).

alternatives.name: Permission Denied
alternatives.reason: The page exists but can't be viewed.

alternatives.name: Error State
alternatives.reason: Only part of a page failed to load.

accessibility: The title ("Page not found") is read first, with the number 404 as supporting information.
The search form uses role="search" and a hidden label so people can search right away.
Keep the site header and footer so there are ways to go elsewhere.
The server really returns a 404 status code so search engines and assistive technology can tell.
